entries.definition: marked by anger or resentment or hostility
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Of a mood rather than an outburst - settled, silent and unpleasant to be near.

entries.definition: marked by skill in deception
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Skill in deceiving, and the skill is half admired - the disapproval is real but not total.
examples: cunning men often pass for wise

entries.definition: obstinate and stupid
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds stupidity to the charge - not just unmoving but unable to see why it should move.

entries.definition: exceptionally bad or displeasing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Moral revulsion - condemns rather than criticises.

entries.definition: extremely silly or stupid
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Withering - stupidity so complete it deserves contempt.

entries.definition: dead
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The neutral official term - legal forms and medical records, no feeling either way.

entries.definition: showing or motivated by sympathy and understanding and generosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Capacity, not just intent: there is room in this person for more than their own concerns.

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Clinical and detached - the word on a chart, not at a graveside.

entries.definition: (used of metals) consisting of or alloyed with inferior metal
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Technical of metals - a grading judgement, not a moral one.

entries.definition: with smiles; in a smiling manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *smiling*: describes the evidence rather than the mood, which is why it can be worn falsely.
examples: the girl reminded her smilingly of their childhood spent together

entries.definition: hasty and without attention to detail; not thorough
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The mildest in the family - the inattention is admitted but hardly blamed.

entries.definition: having undesirable or negative qualities
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain word of disapproval - broad and unemphatic.
examples: his sloppy appearance made a bad impression

entries.definition: suspicious or unduly suspicious or fearful of being displaced by a rival
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Literary and accusing - jealousy given a face and a colour.

entries.definition: in a boastful manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *boastful*: faults the telling rather than the feeling - pride said out loud too often.

entries.definition: (of a female body) healthily plump and vigorous
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Dated approval of a full, healthy figure - warmth with an old-fashioned air.
examples: a generation ago … buxom actresses were popular

entries.definition: with distrust
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *mistrustful*: the plainer twin of *distrustful*, and a shade more tentative.

entries.definition: marked by skill in deception
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The animal metaphor - deceit with the fox's reputation for it.

entries.definition: full of or characterized by loud and nonmusical sounds
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain complaint, and a mild one - noise is expected in most places.

entries.definition: irritable as if suffering from indigestion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British and dated - the liver as the seat of a bad mood.

entries.definition: slow to learn or understand; lacking intellectual acuity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Mild, and it can be jokey - failing to grasp what is plain.
examples: so dense he never understands anything I say to him

entries.definition: free from duties or responsibilities
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Idleness admired - because it is assumed to have been paid for.
examples: even the artist and the sculptor were not regarded … as leisured men

entries.definition: exhibiting childlike simplicity and credulity
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Slightly comic - the eyes wide with belief.

entries.definition: very thin especially from disease or hunger or cold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Suggests thinness carved by hardship, illness or grief - sombre rather than insulting.
examples: a nightmare population of gaunt men and skeletal boys
Months of worry had left him gaunt.

entries.definition: (used colloquially) having the relationship of friends or pals
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: British and blokeish: friendly in a way that insists on being equals.

entries.definition: marked by deliberate deceptiveness especially by pretending one set of feelings and acting under the influence of another
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and personal - the accusation you make to someone's face, or behind their back.

entries.definition: poor enough to need help from others
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames poverty as requiring help; of a person's temperament it means something else entirely.

entries.definition: exhibiting childlike simplicity and credulity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Warm. It keeps the simplicity and drops the accusation.

entries.definition: made dirty or foul
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and disgusted, and it implies an agent: someone fouled this.

entries.definition: having or proceeding from an innately kind disposition
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The hyphenated spelling of the same word, equally warm.

entries.definition: marked by refinement in taste and manners
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praises the work, not the birth - it says the taste was acquired on purpose.

entries.definition: criticize harshly or violently
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Headline language: loud, public and short, with no pretence of fairness.

entries.definition: having a loud resonant metallic sound
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain form, and it names the sound without judging it much.

entries.definition: in an subtle, cunning manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *tricky*: a warning - the skill is in deceiving you.

entries.definition: having a difficult and contrary disposition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Difficulty over small things, and comic rather than frightening.

entries.definition: not in action or at work
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Describes the state, not the person - machinery and money are idle too.

entries.definition: in a courageous manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *courageous*: weightier than 'brave' - implies moral choice, not just nerve.

entries.definition: smiling with happiness or optimism
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Storybook brightness - the smile is pure, quaint delight.
examples: Come to my arms, my beamish boy!

entries.definition: (used of persons and their behavior) not refined; uncouth
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Descriptive and mild - it names an absence rather than an offence.
examples: how can a refined girl be drawn to such an unrefined man?

entries.definition: in a cheerfully buoyant manner
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *chirpy*: british and small-scale, and grating if the hearer is not cheerful too.

entries.definition: given or giving freely
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Describes the habit of giving easily, with no comment on why.

entries.definition: lacking refinement or cultivation or taste
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Coarseness with class in it - the offence is against taste as much as manners.
examples: appealing to the vulgar taste for violence
the vulgar display of the newly rich

entries.definition: brilliantly clever
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Cleverness that sparkles in company.
examples: a play full of scintillating dialogue

entries.definition: resembling a beast; showing lack of human sensibility
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the fault in the absence of ordinary human feeling, one step short of *bestial*.

entries.definition: carefree and happy and lighthearted
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The archaic-sounding form - it carries a deliberate literary flavour.

entries.definition: in a grotesque manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The adverb of *grotesque*: distorted to the point of unsettling - beyond plain ugliness.
examples: behind the house lay two nude figures grotesquely bald, with deliberate knife-slashes marking their bodies

entries.definition: with curiosity
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The adverb of *inquisitive*: praise for a child, and a hint of too many questions for an adult.

entries.definition: ruthless in competition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: No quarter given - ruthlessness the word does not soften.

entries.definition: given to excess in consumption of especially food or drink
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names one of the seven deadly sins; the excess is a moral failure, not an appetite.
examples: over-fed women and their gluttonous husbands

entries.definition: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British slang, jokey and dismissive.

entries.definition: affecting extreme elegance in dress and manner
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Elegance turned into a project, and visibly so.
